association_evidence.supports: MoMA identifies Donald Judd’s Untitled, 1967, lacquer on galvanized iron, accession 298.1997.a–l. Its catalogue specifies twelve units, each 9 × 40 × 31 inches, with nine-inch intervals; its interpretation places the work in Minimalism, describes industrial fabrication, and notes that installation can use fewer units according to ceiling height.

confusion_check.shared_appearances: Sparse surfaces, straight edges and open intervals occur in Modernism, Japandi and Japanese buildings.
confusion_check.discriminating_relationships: The Judd work makes serial units and intervals the subject in a documented Minimal Art context. Ando demonstrates a broader reductive architectural reading. Neither distinction can be reduced to white, empty space or Japanese authorship.
